plotting_plan.title: Incentive-response curves by model
plotting_plan.objective: Line chart with 95% CI: mean contribution share against MPCR (0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.75, 1.25) per model; shaded out-of-dilemma controls; reference lines for the Nash prediction and the human range. Shows H1a and H1b at a glance.

plotting_plan.title: Variance decomposition of contributions
plotting_plan.objective: Stacked horizontal bar per model: share of variance from incentive, paraphrase, framing and seed. Carries the headline signal-to-noise result.

plotting_plan.title: Welfare and payoff by agent type in mixed populations
plotting_plan.objective: Grouped bars: welfare per agent and mean payoff of LLM versus rule agents across compositions.

plotting_plan.title: Conditional-cooperation schedules
plotting_plan.objective: Line chart: own contribution against others' mean contribution from the strategy method, per model, with the 45-degree line.

introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: LLMs are being adopted as agent decision rules in ABMs, and the social simulation community regards validating that practice as its central open problem.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: No study tests, in an N-player public goods game and with current models, whether LLM contributions track the payoff parameter and stay stable under payoff-equivalent rewording. Scope strictly to the linear public goods game with N = 4 and the models in experimental_log.md.
search_directions: Reviews of LLM use in agent-based modelling and their validation practices (done: larooij2026validation, vanhee2026llmabm, edmonds2026when, zhao2026mechanism, liwu2025letitgo)
Foundational experimental evidence on linear public goods games (done: ledyard1995public, isaac1988group, zelmer2003meta, fischbacher2010social, fischbacher2001conditional, andreoni1995warm)
Primary sources for the Smith framing and one behavioural-economics reading (done: smith1776wealth, smith1759moral, ashraf2005smith, vsmith1998two, samuelson1954pure)

related_work_strategy.overview: Three clusters, each ending in the limitation that the present design addresses.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.1 LLM agents in public goods and other social dilemmas
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Describe design parameters (N, endowment, multiplier, action space, prompt context, models, repetitions) of each public goods study and what was varied. Summarise in Table 1.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Single payoff configuration and single context-laden prompt; the only multiplier sweep uses GPT-3.5 with one run per variant and never leaves the dilemma range.
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Sweep of MPCR with out-of-dilemma controls across current model families, with enough replications for intervals.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.2 Framing, prompt sensitivity and strategic-reasoning benchmarks
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Report how structure and context were separated statistically and which manipulations were paraphrase versus framing.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Manipulations change scenario content; paraphrase noise is not measured separately; consistency is judged qualitatively.
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Factorial design that separates payoff-equivalent paraphrases from framings and decomposes variance.

subsections.sota_investigation_mission: State the validation requirements proposed and the documented weaknesses of current practice.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Requirements are stated but few studies supply decision-rule-level audits against external evidence.
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: A decision-rule audit with external grounding in human experiments and explicit robustness analysis.
